theme: So Great Was the Change (Stylistic Inversion)
phoneme_focus: Rhetorical emphasis in inverted clauses; dramatic pitch on fronted elements
grammar_pattern: Stylistic inversion & marked word order for effect

grammar_point.title: Stylistic inversion & marked word order for effect
grammar_point.en: Deliberate inversion and fronting for rhetorical and literary effect beyond standard adverbial inversion: So great was the demand…; Such was the response…; Down came the rain.
grammar_point.ar: القلب والتقديم المتعمّد للأثر البلاغي والأدبي بما يتجاوز القلب الظرفي المعتاد: So great was…؛ Such was…؛ Down came the rain.

vocabulary.example: So great was the demand that stocks ran out.
Such was her influence that all agreed.
Down came the rain in sheets.
Here comes the difficult part.
Into the room walked the director.
Gone are the days of cheap fuel.
Little did they know what awaited.
Hardly had we sat down when the bell rang.
No sooner had he spoken than she left.
Never before had such a crowd gathered.
Not until dawn did the storm ease.
Inversion has a rhetorical effect.
It is an emphatic construction.
The inversion is dramatic.
The prose is highly evocative.
A vivid description held us.
The sentence has a stately cadence.
His prose is elegant.
Marked syntax draws attention.
She ended with a rhetorical flourish.
He spoke with great poise.
Over the valley loomed the peak.
So swiftly did events unfold.
Through the hall resounded the applause.
Upon the city descended a hush.
So firmly did the belief prevail.
So profound was the silence.
Such was the immense scale.
Stark was the contrast between them.
So momentous was the decision.
Such was the tale that all sat spellbound.

Saturday.prompt: Make five dramatic statements with 'So great was…' and 'Such was…'.

Sunday.prompt: Describe scenes with fronted verbs ('Into the room walked…', 'Down came…').

Monday.prompt: Tell a story using 'Hardly had…', 'No sooner…', 'Little did…'.

Tuesday.prompt: Reflect on change using 'Gone are the days…' and 'Never before…'.

Wednesday.prompt: Paint a vivid, evocative scene using stylistic inversion.

Thursday.prompt: Tell a partner a dramatic anecdote using marked word order for effect.

Friday.prompt: Perform an evocative narrative passage (12-14 sentences) rich in stylistic inversion.

writing_prompts: Write five 'So + adjective + was… that…' / 'Such was… that…' sentences.
Write three sentences with a fronted verb of motion ('Down came…', 'Into the room walked…').
Write a narrative opening using 'Hardly had…', 'No sooner…', 'Little did…'.
Write two 'Gone are the days…' / 'Never before…' reflections.
Write an evocative descriptive paragraph using stylistic inversion.
Write a dramatic short narrative that deploys marked word order for effect.
